about_quran.title: The Quran
about_quran.whatIsQuran: The Quran is the revealed word of Allah in Arabic and the central scripture of Islam. Muslims believe it was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the Angel Jibril, beginning in Makkah and continuing over approximately 23 years.
about_quran.meaningOfQuran: Qur'an means recitation or that which is recited.
about_quran.purpose: Guidance for humanity in faith, worship, morality, justice, repentance, patience, gratitude and accountability before Allah.
about_quran.preservation: The Quran was memorized and written during the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It was collected into a single compilation during Abu Bakr's caliphate and standardized copies were distributed during Uthman ibn Affan's caliphate.

history.makkanPeriod: Early revelation emphasized tawhid, resurrection, accountability, worship, patience, moral character and lessons from earlier prophets and peoples.
history.hijrah: The migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE marks the beginning of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
history.madanianPeriod: Madinan revelation addressed worship and community life in greater detail, including family matters, contracts, justice, charity, fasting, warfare and social responsibilities.
history.compilationUnderAbuBakr: After the Battle of Yamamah and the deaths of many Quran memorizers, Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه commissioned a collection of Quranic material, led by Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه.
history.standardizationUnderUthman: Uthman ibn Affan رضي الله عنه commissioned standardized copies and distributed them to major centers to reduce disputes over recitation forms.
history.preservationToday: The Quran continues to be transmitted through memorization, written manuscripts, printed mushafs and established recitation traditions.

statistics.note: Verse, word, letter and sajdah counts can vary according to counting convention, script, recitation tradition or scholarly school. 6,236 is the common Hafs/Kufan verse-count convention.

motherOfQuran.name: Al-Fatiha
motherOfQuran.note: Traditionally called Umm al-Quran, Umm al-Kitab and As-Sab al-Mathani.

heartOfQuran.name: Ya-Sin
heartOfQuran.note: Popularly called the Heart of the Quran in traditional literature; this is an honorific description, not a Quranic statement.

longestVerse.name: Ayat al-Dayn
longestVerse.description: The longest verse; it discusses recording debts and financial contracts.

shortestVerse.note: Claims depend on whether letters, words or orthographic conventions are counted.

longestWord.meaning: And We gave you drink from it.

mostCommonArabicLetter.name: Alif
mostCommonArabicLetter.note: Alif is consistently reported as the most frequent basic Arabic letter; exact counts vary by orthographic method.

leastCommonArabicLetter.name: Ẓāʾ
leastCommonArabicLetter.note: Common Quranic letter-frequency analyses identify Ẓāʾ as the least frequent; exact counts vary by orthographic method.

makkiSurahs.description: Surahs classified as Makki were predominantly revealed before the Hijrah; individual verses may have different classifications.

madaniSurahs.description: Surahs classified as Madani were predominantly revealed after the Hijrah; individual verses may have different classifications.

lastRevelation.note: Scholars differ over the final verse revealed. Al-Baqarah 2:281 is one commonly cited view.

surahsReportedAsRevealedMoreThanOnce.note: Classical works also report repeated revelation for certain verses or passages. Present this as a scholarly report, not an undisputed fact.

onlyWomanNamedExplicitly.name: Maryam
onlyWomanNamedExplicitly.note: Maryam is the only woman mentioned by personal name in the Quran.

onlyCompanionNamedExplicitly.name: Zayd ibn Harithah
onlyCompanionNamedExplicitly.note: Zayd ibn Harithah رضي الله عنه is the companion explicitly named in the Quran.

whatIsInQuran: Stories of prophets and earlier nations
Patience, gratitude and reliance upon Allah
Guidance for individual and community life

beautyOfQuran.description: The beauty of the Quran is experienced through its language, rhythm, imagery, structure, depth of meaning, moral guidance, spiritual impact and recitation.
beautyOfQuran.note: Beauty is devotional and literary rather than a measurable statistic.
